page: Microsoft Azure D32_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and provisioned via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor comprising 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes hardware acceleration extensions such as AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic AES instructions. This instance features no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent filesystems.

Benchmark testing places the D32_v4 consistently within the average middle-tier range across general compute and memory metrics. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,337.0 and a single-core score of 1,245.0, alongside a multi-core stress-ng metric of 29,790.94. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 86.61 GB/sec with write speeds of 33.96 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks highlight a static web serving throughput of 18.85 GB/sec and a Redis SET operational rate of 26.15 million operations per second. In machine learning inference evaluations, small 135M parameter models process prompts at 1,080.86 tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly to 4.36 tokens per second on large 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

The resource profile provides dependable compute density and consistent memory bandwidth without incurring the cost premiums associated with memory-optimized or accelerator-backed tiers. Because the instance contains no local ephemeral or NVMe disks, disk I/O performance relies on attached storage configurations. The server is well configured for production workloads requiring stable multithreading and balanced memory, including relational databases, Redis caching layers, web server pools, CI/CD compilation, and enterprise backend applications.

It features AVX-512 vector support and AES cryptography, while omitting bundled local storage and hardware GPU acceleration.
